text:
anya: Quick follow-up from the compact-cursor RFC review — I sketched a few concrete options for the resume token shape and how SDKs should expose it. TL;DR: we should prefer an opaque, verifiable token that also carries retry/hint metadata, not a user-parsable JSON blob.

matt: Curious — what's the downside to structured JSON? Easier debugging and we can evolve fields.

anya: Main problems: 1) cross-lang stability — folks will start parsing fields in Python/TS/Go which blocks changing internals, 2) security/PII risk if customers accidentally include request context, and 3) accidental coupling when apps start relying on ordering. Opaque token solves those.

sarah: +1 for opaque. Practical question: how do we include retry hints (e.g., suggested backoff window, server side idempotency nonce) for transports without adding separate headers?

anya: My proposal: compact token = base64url(gzip) of an internal proto with a version byte + signature. SDKs get helpers: `ResumeToken.parse()` -> gives `ResumeMetadata { version, nonce, seq, hint_ms }` but the canonical token remains opaque. We only expose parsed metadata read-only.

oscar: Implementation-wise, signing is fine but key rotation is a pain esp for private deployments. Can we avoid cryptographic signature and instead do an HMAC with a rotated shared key?

anya: HMAC is what I had in mind. For Redwood-hosted tokens we HMAC with service key; for Dedicated/Private we HMAC with tenant key (deployed via KMS). If key absent, token has a `unsigned` flag and SDKs treat it as best-effort. We should document downgrade behavior.

matt: SDK ergonomics: Python/TS/Go surfaces differ. Suggestion: expose minimal helpers: `client.resume_from(token)` and `token.metadata()`; avoid leaking proto classes to users. Keep token a string throughout.

sarah: Agreed. For Python, returning a small dataclass is nice: `ResumeData(version:int, hint_ms:int|None, nonce:str|None)`. For TS -> `interface ResumeData`. For Go -> simple struct. But we must ensure zero alloc hot paths for streaming.

oscar: Retry semantics interplay: if a resume token contains `seq` and we see a partial response, do we let SDKs retry automatically or surface to app? My vote: automatic transparent retry for unary/paginated fetches but not for streaming unless SDK has explicit `autoResume=true` flag. Streams are delicate.

anya: Yes, automatic resume for idempotent operations only. We'll rely on server-provided `idempotency` bit in token metadata and the SDK will only auto-resume when that bit set. For streams: default = no auto resume; provide `stream.resume_policy = { auto: boolean, max_retries: int }`.

matt: Transport choices — gRPC streaming vs HTTP/2 SSE vs plain HTTP polling. Any preference? If we keep cursor token small, polling with a resume header is simplest for SDKs behind proxies.

sarah: Agnostic but note: Go clients in some infra prefer gRPC; JS (browser) can't use gRPC native easily so HTTP streaming fallback required. So SDKs should normalize: connection layer provides abstraction `Connection.resume(token)` and each language implements underlying transport.

anya: Exactly. Keep SDK surface transport-agnostic. Provide `ResumeToken` string + helper functions and a transport adapter interface: `Resume(token)`, `PollNext()`, `OpenStream()`. Document expected semantics.

oscar: Backoff: servers embed a `hint_ms` but SDKs should still run standard exponential-with-jitter. Hint becomes a suggested minimum delay to avoid hot-loop retries. Also add `retry_budget` field in token for cross-request rate limiting?

sarah: `retry_budget` sounds useful but introduces server accounting complexity. Maybe keep it optional for now. If present, SDKs will treat it as advisory.

matt: Tests: we should add cross-lang conformance tests that exercise token rotation, unsigned tokens, missing fields, and malformed tokens. ci-bot: can we add a matrix job for python/js/go that runs the token doc tests?

ci-bot: @anya I created a pipeline job: `token-interop-matrix` — runs on PRs that touch resume/token code. Details: https://ci.internal/jobs/token-interop-matrix

anya: Nice. Action items: 1) I'll draft an implementation PR for server proto + HMAC token format. 2) @matt please sketch the SDK helper API for the three languages (keeps token as string, exposes `parse_metadata` and `resume_from`). 3) @sarah add interop test cases and a minimal HTTP fallback transport adapter for JS. 4) @oscar write a short doc about key rotation and unsigned token policy for Dedicated/Private.

matt: I can have SDK sketches by EOD tomorrow.

sarah: Will add tests next sprint.

oscar: I'll draft key rotation doc and include KMS examples.

anya: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC follow-up PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:

anya: (one more note) Keep the resume token under 512 bytes — many browsers/proxies clamp headers. If payload exceeds, we'll fall back to a server-side resume ID reference.

matt: Good call.

sarah: If anybody wants to pair on the JS fallback adapter, I can pair tomorrow morning.

oscar: +1

ci-bot: Thread archived by CI retention policy after inactivity.
